title: WPSS/144/2024 of MAHENDRA PAL SINGH GREWAL Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
2026:UHC:4003
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE MANOJ KUMAR TIWARI
Writ Petition Service Single No. 144 of 2024
21 May, 2026
Dr. Mahendra Pal Singh Grewal --Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others --Respondents
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
There is no representation for the petitioner.
Mr. K.N. Joshi, Deputy Advocate General for the State of
Uttarakhand.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
JUDGMENT
Petitioner was appointed as Assistant Teacher
in A.N. Jha, Government Inter College, Rudrapur in the
year 1986 for teaching Punjabi language, however, he
thereafter accepted appointment as Professor (Hindi) in
Sri Gurunanak Khalsa Degree College, Ganganagar
(Rajasthan) w.e.f. 18.11.1988, without resigning from
the post of Assistant Teacher in A.N. Jha, Government
Inter College, Rudrapur.
2. According to petitioner, he served as
Professor at Ganganagar till 27.11.1995 and thereafter
he re-joined duties in A.N. Jha, Government Inter
College, Rudrapur on 07.03.1996. Petitioner retired
from service after attaining age of superannuation on
31.03.2006.
3. By means of this writ petition, petitioner has
sought the following reliefs:
1

2026:UHC:4003
"(i) To issue a writ, order or direction in nature of
mandamus directing the respondents to grant the
pension to the petitioner for his complete service,
along with 12% interest, for the delayed payment,
from the date of his superannuation till the date of
actual payment for the delayed payment.
(ii) To issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
mandamus directing the respondents to give the
retiral benefits to the petitioner for his complete
service, along with 12% interest, for the delayed
payment, from the date of his superannuation till the
date of actual payment for the delayed payment."
4. A counter affidavit is filed by Mr. Daya
Shaknakar Pandey on behalf of respondent nos. 2 & 3.
Para no. 3 of the said counter affidavit is reproduced
below:-
"3. That the petitioner was appointed in the
office of District Inspector of School Nainital vide
order no. 9 dated 2.8.1986 in CT cadre as Assistant
Teacher (Punjabi). The petitioner has joined in
Government Inter College, Rudrapur, Nainital on
7.8.1986. The petitioner after his first appointment
on 7.8.1986 to 28.8.1988 has posted as Assistant
Teacher in Government Inter College, Rudrapur,
Nainital. The petitioner after his total services from
5.1.1988 to 30.4.1988 (total 1 month 7 days) was on
leave without pay and from 8.7.1988 to 4.8.1988
(total 28 days) was on medical leave.
During appointment as Assistant Teacher, the
petitioner without taking permission from
department, the petitioner has worked as Lecturer
(Hindi) in Government Inter College Gadarpur from
5.1.1988 to 30.4.1988 on part time basis. It is
further submitted that form 18.11.1988 to
27.11.1995 the petitioner has worked in Shri Guru
Nanak Khalsa Degree College Ganganagar,
Rajasthan. In this regard the petitioner has never
applied for no objection certificate. The petitioner
from 28.8.1988 to 6.3.1996 was absent from
Government Inter College Rudrapur Nainital without
any permission and information to department. As
per office record of the school, the warning letter was
issued to petitioner on 29.7.1992 despite that the
petitioner has not joined in Government Inter College
Rudrapur Nainital.
On 8.3.1996 the Additional Education Director,
Kumaun Division, Nainital due to mistake has given
2

2026:UHC:4003
promotion to petitioner on Assistant Teacher LT
Grade, but due to long absent from department
finally the promotion of the petitioner was cancelled.
The District Inspector of School Nainital vide letter
no. 2/93 dated 15.4.1996 on the ground that the
petitioner is absent till 10.8.1992 as well as absent
from 28.8.1988 to 6.3.1996 there was not provision
to sanction leave for 8 years. The services of the
petitioner were terminated.
Against termination order dated 15.4.1996 the
petitioner has filed a petition no. 416/1997 before
Hon'ble Public Services Tribunal, Uttar Pradesh. After
creation of the State of Uttarakhand, the petitioner
was transferred and the Public Services Tribunal vide
order dated 1.6.2011 passed following order in the
matter of petitioner:-
"The petition is allowed. Opposite parties are
directed to pay the petitioner regular salary w.e.f. of
08-03-1996 till the age of superannuation of the
petitioner of the post of Assistant Teacher in Punjabi
in the pay Scale of Rs 1350-2070 as revised from
time to time along with all consequential benefits. No
order as to Costs."
Thereafter the State Government has filed a
writ petition against decision passed by Hon'ble
Public Service Tribunal titled as Writ Petition No.
58/2012. Vide order dated 6.12.2016 the Hon'ble
High Court dismissed the Special Appeal of the State
Government and confirmed the order passed by
Hon'ble Tribunal dated 1.6.2011, thereafter in
compliance of the order passed by the Public Service
Tribunal as well as the order passed by Hon'ble High
Court of Uttarakhand, the department has paid
salary of the petitioner for the period of 8.3.1996 to
31.3.2004 (Rs. 9,79,937/-).
The petitioner again filed a Claim Petition No.
25/DB/2018, Dr. Mahendra Pal Singh Grewal Vs
State of Uttarakhand & others by which the
petitioner has prayed before Public Services Tribunal
that to issue a writ, order or direction to the
respondents to pay all the retiral benefits to
petitioner as such pension from 1.4.2006 to till date
and future pension, gratuity, commutation of
pension, GPF, leave encashment, GIS and other
benefits, which are payable to petitioner on the date
of his superannuation along with 18% interest per
annum from 1.4.2006 till the date of actual payment.
The Hon'ble Public Service Tribunal vide order dated
3.8.2018 allowed the petition of the petitioner.
The petitioner has filed the Execution
3

2026:UHC:4003
Application before Hon'ble Public Service Tribunal, in
compliance of that the Chief Treasury Officer Udham
Singh Nagar vide letter no. 337 dated 9.12.2019 paid
all retiral benefits, pension, gratuity, GPF and earned
leave of the petitioner. The petitioner has annexed
Annexure No.3 before Hon'ble Public Service Tribunal
and in Annexure-3 annexed before Public Service
Tribunal the petitioner has admitted that the pension
gratuity matter of the petitioner has been decided.
The petitioner has filed present writ petition for
granting 12% interest on the payment of gratuity
and pension as the petitioner has been granted the
benefit of retiral dues and pension so the petition of
the petitioner is liable to be dismissed."
5. Learned State Counsel submits that whatever
was due to petitioner, has been paid. He refers to the
application submitted by petitioner before Public
Service Tribunal, which is enclosed as Annexure-3 to
the counter affidavit of respondent nos. 2 & 3. Perusal
of said document reveals that petitioner stated that the
issue of payment of his pension/gratuity is resolved,
therefore, the case pending before learned Public
Service Tribunal may be closed. Learned State Counsel
submits that the said application was submitted by
petitioner when all his pending dues were paid to him.
6. This Court vide order dated 04.05.2026
granted time to learned senior counsel appearing for
petitioner to get clear instructions regarding the
document enclosed as Annexure CA-3 to the counter
affidavit.
7. Today, there is no representation for the
petitioner.
8. Since petitioner himself submitted application
before Public Services Tribunal stating that the issue
regarding pension and gratuity with the department
4

2026:UHC:4003
has been resolved, therefore, he cannot later turn-around for staking claim for pension for the entire
period, in disregard of the fact that he served at
Ganganagar during the interregnum. In last sub para of
para no. 3 of the counter affidavit, filed on behalf of
respondent nos. 2 & 3 also, it is stated that pension-gratuity matter of the petitioner was settled, therefore,
writ petition filed by petitioner is liable to be dismissed.
The averment made in para 3 of the counter affidavit
remains un-rebutted. Thus, this Court has no other
option, but to accept the averment made in para 3 of
the counter affidavit as correct
9. Even otherwise also, petitioner cannot be
given pension for the entire length of service i.e.
between 1986 till 2006, when he did not render any
service in A.N. Jha Government Inter College, Rudrapur
for more than seven years.
10. Learned State Counsel submits that petitioner
is being paid pension for the entire period he served in
A.N. Jha Inter College i.e., eleven years nine months
and sixteen days.
11. In view of the aforesaid facts, the relief, as
claimed by petitioner, cannot be granted. The writ
petition thus fails and is dismissed. There shall be no
order as to costs.
(Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.)
Dt: 21ST May, 2026
